# Auxiliary input for factory radio

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Cut ribbon cables, tin and solder an auxiliary donor cable to pins, then run the wire through the radio. [t1489]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove every visible screw from the radio faceplate.
2. Pull and pry until the entire radio assembly comes apart.
3. Turn the unit over to locate the connectors for the CD player ribbon cable.
4. Cut an AUX cable in half while identifying which wire corresponds to each channel.
5. Tin the exposed ends of both cut cable pieces.
6. Solder one end of the donor cable to the L pin on the bottom of the radio board.
7. Solder that same piece's other end to the R pin on the bottom of the radio board.
8. Solder the second half of the donor cable to the ground pin on the bottom of the radio board.
9. Run the new audio wire through the metal case of the radio before securing it permanently.
10. Reassemble all components and place the unit back into the truck.
11. Insert a CD into the player and switch the source to CD audio mode.
12. Cut the second connector from the left on the ribbon cable connecting to the board.
13. Cut the third connector from the left on that same ribbon cable connection.
14. Punch a hole in the top of the storage pocket located in front of the shifter.

_Procedure reported by [t1489]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-add-aux-input-to-factory-radio.9375/>_

## Tools

- Soldering iron [t1489]
- Tin (solder) [t1489]

## Parts

- Auxiliary cable: Old monitor cable or custom female jack mount [t1489]
- Ribbon cable connectors: To cut if disabling CD input [t1489]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a test video with distinct left/right channels to identify wire colors. [t1489]
- Run the new AUX cable through the radio's metal case before soldering to ensure it fits later. [t1489]
